rationale: The golden_rejected issue is present: evaluate.py's load_traces() uses csv.DictReader against inputs/traces.csv, but the actual traces.csv file (as authored/shipped) contains prose/derivation text and a markdown code fence wrapping the real CSV data rather than a clean CSV with the header row as its first line. This causes DictReader to choke with KeyError: 'trial_id' identically on both the golden run (expected pass, got fail) and the vulnerable baseline run (expected fail, got fail-for-the-wrong-reason), so the check discriminates nothing. Because the golden run cannot even reach the FR/SR logic, mutation_score is 0.0 and not meaningful, and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0. Additionally, the input_artifact_not_filename issue flags that public_spec.input_artifacts references 'traces.csv' inconsistently with the actual malformed content the evaluator opens. This is squarely an evaluation/artifact-packaging bug, not a specification or golden-solution defect: the golden report content is correct per the hidden spec and ground truth, and the interface/timing model is already precisely pinned. The fix belongs to whichever artifact actually emits the malformed inputs/traces.csv file consumed by evaluate.py -- that file's content in the artifact bundle is the derivation scratchpad, not clean data -- so this is flagged as an evaluation_framework/case_artifacts packaging defect that must be corrected before mutation scoring can be trusted.
revision_instructions: Fix the FR1 SETUP failure causing golden_rejected: 'evaluate.py: SETUP: failed to parse inputs/traces.csv: 'trial_id''. The evaluator's load_traces() must be able to parse inputs/traces.csv as a directly loadable CSV via csv.DictReader with header row 'trial_id,secret_operand,cycle_index,mul_en,done' as the literal first line of the file -- no surrounding prose, no markdown code-fence markers (```), no derivation commentary before or after the data rows. Regenerate/repackage inputs/traces.csv as a plain, well-formed CSV data file only (strip all narrative text and fence markers), matching exactly the shape trace_manifest.json documents (18 trials x 10 rows each, columns trial_id,secret_operand,cycle_index,mul_en,done). Do not alter evaluate.py's parsing contract to accommodate markdown-wrapped input; instead ensure the input artifact itself is clean, since public_spec.input_artifacts declares traces.csv as a plain reference data file that participants and the evaluator both read verbatim. After the fix, re-run the differential harness: the golden submission must produce all '[TEST] PASS' lines (exit 0), and the shipped naive baseline submission must produce '[TEST] FAIL' specifically on FR3, SR1, and SR2 (and ideally SR3) per the acceptance criteria. Also resolve the input_artifact_not_filename warning by confirming metadata.json/public_spec.input_artifacts references the exact plain filename 'traces.csv' consistent with the corrected file. Once golden passes cleanly, regenerate mutants and confirm mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score are non-zero, i.e., each FR/SR check actually distinguishes correct from corrupted/insecure submissions.
